text:
Noah Rivera: Quick UX question — should a saved per-route query store "preview sampling" state so the dashboard shows the same aggregate numbers when you load it later?
Asha Kapoor: I'm leaning no for default saves. People expect saved filters to be declarative, not capture transient sampling. But we should offer a snapshot option.
Evan Brooks: +1. Maybe two modes: "Save Filter" vs "Save Snapshot". Snapshot freezes the preview numbers, filter save just stores the filter expression and recomputes on load.
Riley Park: From rollout perspective, snapshots help when we A/B compare telemetry across model variants. If we don't freeze sampling, comparisons become noisy.
Noah Rivera: Good point. UX challenge: how to surface that without scaring users. Propose copy: "Save as snapshot (captures current sampling, routing and model variant) — useful for audits" and a short inline link "why snapshot?"
Asha Kapoor: Also add an expiry on snapshots? If model/route policies change, stale snapshots might be misleading. Maybe auto-expire after N days with a banner that says "snapshot references model v3.2 (now v3.4)".
Evan Brooks: Implementation detail: snapshots will need to persist metadata: model_version, route_config_hash, effective_sampling_rate, quota_snapshot. That increases object size but it's necessary.
Noah Rivera: Telemetry ask: can we tag every saved-query-load event with which sampling mode was used and whether a fallback routing occurred? That helps us measure how often consoles show different results than live.
QA-bot: QA-bot: test task created: console/savedquery/snapshot-consistency-check — will run synthetic loads against snapshots and record mismatch rate :white_check_mark:
Riley Park: One more: for per-model views in the console, show a "route impact" panel that lists top routes that would be affected by a model change (e.g., quantization, lower capacity). This would help model rollouts.
Asha Kapoor: Nice. That panel could show estimated token delta, % of traffic affected, and quota thresholds where fallback would trigger.
Evan Brooks: Tech caveat: estimating token delta requires simulating prefix caching and route filters. We can provide a heuristic (95th percentile historical prefix length) and mark as "estimate".
Noah Rivera: UX microcopy: "Estimated token change — influenced by cache and filter effectiveness" and tooltip linking to docs.
Asha Kapoor: For saved query previews, add a compact "cost forecast": live tokens per minute, projected tokens at current sampling, and cost band (low/medium/high) with a color pill. Users like quick signals.
Riley Park: Regarding routing fallbacks — show an audit trail in the saved query details: when a saved query was executed and which model served it (primary vs fallback). That'll help debugging when results differ.
Evan Brooks: We'll need a lightweight event for each execution: saved_query_id, execution_ts, model_served, fallback_reason(optional). Keep payload tiny (strings/enums) so we don't blow up analytics storage.
Noah Rivera: How about a console toggle for "show historical executions" that queries these small events to populate the audit trail? Default off.
Asha Kapoor: Good. Also add a signal in the saved queries list: a small icon if any execution used a fallback in the last 7 days. Click it to see details.
QA-bot: QA-bot: added tests for fallback-icon visibility across different execution histories. :white_check_mark:
Riley Park: One policy question: if a saved query references a route that later loses access (e.g., deleted), should we retain the snapshot or mark as orphaned? I vote retain but mark as orphaned with warning.
Noah Rivera: Retain. We should let users download the snapshot (JSON) and maybe reattach to a new route. Also provide a "re-evaluate snapshot" button to run the saved filter against current configs and show differences.
Asha Kapoor: UX flow for re-evaluate: show a diff card with three columns: snapshot numbers, live numbers, delta. Add buttons: "save as new snapshot" and "update saved filter".
Evan Brooks: Backend note: re-evaluate should be a background job to avoid blocking the console. Return short job id and poll. Limit to small sample by default.
Noah Rivera: Action list: Evan to design compact telemetry event and re-eval job API; Asha to write snapshot UI copy and mockups; Riley to specify audit trail columns; QA-bot to add automated checks. I'll create a short RFC for snapshot semantics.
Evan Brooks: I'll also add a quick CLI to export a snapshot and run re-eval: `ri snapshots export <id> --recheck`.
Asha Kapoor: One more tiny UX ask: when saving a filter, show a one-line preview: "preview (n=12k tokens/min, sampling=0.12)" so users know the immediate cost impact.
Noah Rivera: Love it. Let's sync next Tue for the mock review.
QA-bot: QA-bot: RFC checklist created and assigned to Evan/Asha/Riley :white_check_mark:
